description: Is dagron itself healthy and fast: engines up, clock and claim state, backlog, and how long the scheduler takes to dispatch a task, collect a result and complete a reconcile pass.

panels.title: Engines up
panels.description: Selected engines that answered their last scrape.

panels.title: Clock
panels.description: Wall-clock confidence stamped on new runs. Worst value across the selected engines.

panels.title: Claims
panels.description: Whether DAGRON_PRESSURE_FILE is holding new task claims at zero on any selected engine.

panels.title: Job failures
panels.description: Tasks that exhausted their retries, as a share of all finished tasks, over the last 5 minutes.

targets.expr: sum(rate(scheduler_tasks_failed_total{namespace=~"$namespace", job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[5m])) / (sum(rate(scheduler_tasks_succeeded_total{namespace=~"$namespace", job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[5m])) + sum(rate(scheduler_tasks_failed_total{namespace=~"$namespace", job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[5m])))

panels.title: Dispatch p95
panels.description: 95th percentile time from a task becoming claimable to being handed to a worker, over the last 5 minutes.

panels.title: Result p95
panels.description: 95th percentile time a finished task waits for the reconcile loop to collect its result.

panels.title: Tick p95
panels.description: 95th percentile duration of one reconcile-loop pass. Above one second the loop is falling behind.

panels.title: Queue depth
panels.description: Ready tasks waiting for a worker.

panels.title: Engine up
panels.description: Whether Prometheus could scrape each engine.

panels.title: Clock confidence per engine
panels.description: The confidence each engine stamps on new runs.

panels.title: Claims paused per engine
panels.description: Whether the pressure file is holding claims at zero.

panels.title: Backlog
panels.description: Ready tasks waiting for a worker, and the age of the oldest one.

panels.title: Run deadlines
panels.description: Hard: runs failed by run_timeout_secs. Soft: SLA alerts raised by deadline, where the run keeps going.

panels.title: Leaked workloads and clock steps
panels.description: Remote jobs the engine could not tear down, pods or containers the fleet sweep deleted because their task was no longer live, and wall-clock steps the detector caught.

panels.title: Dispatch latency
panels.description: Task became claimable (scheduled_at) to handed to a worker: claim wait, tick pacing and dispatch preparation. A retry's clock starts at its due time, so backoff is not counted.

panels.title: Dispatch latency distribution
panels.description: Dispatches per bucket in each interval. A second band above the main one means some tasks are waiting a full tick.

panels.title: Dispatches inside a latency budget
panels.description: Share of dispatches that finished within each bound. Read this as an SLO: pick the line that matches your target and alert when it drops.

panels.title: Result wait
panels.description: Executor finished to result drained by the reconcile loop. Rises when the loop is busy.

panels.title: Reconcile tick duration
panels.description: One pass of recover, advance, dispatch, collect and reap. The dashed line is the one-second alert threshold.

panels.title: Reconcile tick distribution
panels.description: Ticks per duration bucket in each interval.

panels.title: Claim batch size
panels.description: Tasks taken per non-empty claim. A p95 pinned at WORKER_COUNT means every claim fills the pool and work is queueing behind it.

title: dagron — health and latency
